You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.
  - Specify dependencies between tasks.
  - Schedule tasks to run at a specific time.
- Process interaction
  - Easy output inspection.
  - Send input to running processes.
  - Pause/resume tasks, when you need some processing power right NOW!
- Task groups (multiple queues)
  - Each group can have several tasks running in parallel.
  - Pause/start tasks by a group.
- Background process execution
  - The `pueued` daemon runs in the background. No need to be logged in.
  - Commands are executed in their respective working directories.
  - The current environment variables are copied when adding a task.
  - Commands are run in a shell which allows the full feature set of shell coding.
- Consistency
  - The queue is always saved to disk and restored on kill/system crash.
  - Logs are persisted onto the disk and survive a crash.
- Miscellaneous
  - A callback hook to, for instance, set up desktop notifications.
  - JSON output for `log` and `status` if you want to display info about tasks in another program.
  - A `wait` subcommand to wait for specific tasks, a group (or everything) to finish.
- A lot more. Check the -h options for each subcommand for detailed options.
- Cross Platform
  - Linux is fully supported and battle-tested.
  - MacOS is fully supported and on par with Linux.
  - Windows is fully supported and working fine for quite a while.

## What Pueue is **not**

Pueue is **not** designed to be a heavy-duty programmable (scriptable) task scheduler/executor.

The focus of `pueue` lies on human interaction, i.e. it's supposed to be used by a real person on some kind of OS.

Due to this, the feature set of `pueue` and `pueued` as well as their implementation and architecture have been kept simple by design!
Even though it can be scripted to some degree, it hasn't been built for heavy-duty work like hundreds of tasks!

## Installation

Pueue can be installed via your system's package manager, or by downloading prebuilt binaries from the [release page](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/releases).

## How to Use it

Pueue consists of two components:
- `pueued` - The daemon that runs in the background and manages your tasks
- `pueue` - The client used to interact with the daemon

### Basic Commands

```text
Interact with the Pueue daemon

Usage: pueue [OPTIONS] [COMMAND]

Commands:
  add            Enqueue a task for execution.
                     There're many different options when scheduling a task.
                     Check the individual option help texts for more information.

                     Furthermore, please remember that scheduled commands are executed via your system shell.
                     This means that the command needs proper shell escaping.
                     The safest way to preserve shell escaping is to surround your command with quotes, for example:
                     pueue add 'ls $HOME && echo "Some string"'
  remove         Remove tasks from the list. Running or paused tasks need to be killed first
  switch         Switches the queue position of two commands. Only works on queued and stashed commands
  stash          Stashed tasks won't be automatically started. You have to enqueue them or start them by hand
  enqueue        Enqueue stashed tasks. They'll be handled normally afterwards
  start          Resume operation of specific tasks or groups of tasks.
                     By default, this resumes the default group and all its tasks.
                     Can also be used force-start specific tasks.
  restart        Restart failed or successful task(s).
                     By default, identical tasks will be created and enqueued, but it's possible to restart in-place.
                     You can also edit a few properties, such as the path and the command, before restarting.
  pause          Either pause running tasks or specific groups of tasks.
                     By default, pauses the default group and all its tasks.
                     A paused queue (group) won't start any new tasks.
  kill           Kill specific running tasks or whole task groups..
                     Kills all tasks of the default group when no ids or a specific group are provided.
  send           Send something to a task. Useful for sending confirmations such as 'y\n'
  edit           Edit the command, path or label of a stashed or queued task.
                     By default only the command is edited.
                     Multiple properties can be added in one go.
  group          Use this to add or remove groups.
                     By default, this will simply display all known groups.
  status         Display the current status of all tasks
  format-status  Accept a list or map of JSON pueue tasks via stdin and display it just like "pueue status".
                     A simple example might look like this:
                     pueue status --json | jq -c '.tasks' | pueue format-status
  log            Display the log output of finished tasks.
                     Only the last few lines will be shown by default.
                     If you want to follow the output of a task, please use the "follow" subcommand.
  follow         Follow the output of a currently running task. This command works like "tail -f"
  wait           Wait until tasks are finished.
                     By default, this will wait for all tasks in the default group to finish.
                     Note: This will also wait for all tasks that aren't somehow 'Done'.
                     Includes: [Paused, Stashed, Locked, Queued, ...]
  clean          Remove all finished tasks from the list
  reset          Kill all tasks, clean up afterwards and reset EVERYTHING!
  shutdown       Remotely shut down the daemon. Should only be used if the daemon isn't started by a service manager
  parallel       Set the amount of allowed parallel tasks
                     By default, adjusts the amount of the default group.
                     No tasks will be stopped, if this is lowered.
                     This limit is only considered when tasks are scheduled.
  completions    Generates shell completion files. This can be ignored during normal operations
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
  -v, --verbose...         Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv)
      --color <COLOR>      Colorize the output; auto enables color output when connected to a tty [default: auto] [possible values: auto, never, always]
  -c, --config <CONFIG>    If provided, Pueue only uses this config file. This path can also be set via the "PUEUE_CONFIG_PATH" environment variable. The commandline option overwrites the environment variable!
  -p, --profile <PROFILE>  The name of the profile that should be loaded from your config file
  -h, --help               Print help
  -V, --version            Print version
```

## Similar Projects

#### slurm

[Slurm](https://slurm.schedmd.com/overview.html) is a feature rich and widely used cluster management and scheduling system.
If you find yourself in the need for complex setups such as multiple worker pools or distributed nodes, slurm will be much better suited than Pueue.

#### GNU Parallel

A robust and featureful parallel processor with text-based joblog and n-retries. [GNU Parallel](https://www.gnu.org/software/parallel/parallel_tutorial.html) is able to scale to multi-host parallelization and has complex code to have deep integration across different tools and shells, as well as other advanced features. `Pueue` differentiates itself from GNU Parallel by focusing more on visibility across many different long running commands, and creating a central location for commands to be stored, rather than GNU Parallel's focus on chunking a specific task.

#### Pm2

[pm2](https://pm2.keymetrics.io/docs/usage/quick-start/) is a process management tool, whose focus is more on management of recurring and long-living tasks.
It seems to be quite mature and has a rich interface.

#### nq

A very lightweight job queue system which advertises no setup, maintenance, supervision, or otherwise long-running background processes. \
[Link to project](https://github.com/leahneukirchen/nq)

#### task-spooler

_task spooler_ is a Unix batch system where the tasks spooled run one after the other. \
Links to [ubuntu manpage](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/xenial/man1/tsp.1.html) and a [fork on Github](https://github.com/xenogenesi/task-spooler).

def test(s):
    r=subprocess.run(["./executable","wait","--help"], capture_output=True, text=True)
    print(r.stdout)
    print(r.stderr)

import subprocess, os, tempfile
def check_status(s):
    e=os.environ.copy()
    e["XDG_CONFIG_HOME"]=tempfile.mkdtemp()

for s in ["queued","stashed","paused","running","success","failed","done","locked","success","failure","fail","succeed","Succeeded","Failed","Done","Locked","Stashed","Paused","Queued","Running","ququed",""]:
    check_status(s)

            conn.settimeout(4)

                        print(f"    {str(d)[:2000]!r}")

                    payload2=encode_cbor({"Success": "edited ok"})
                    conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(payload2))+payload2)
                    conn.settimeout(1)
                    try: conn.recv(8)
                    except: pass
                elif len(h3)==0:
                    print("  closed after first resp")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"  no second: {e}")
            conn.close()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"server err {e}")
        finally:
            srv.close()
    st=threading.Thread(target=server)

    os.chmod(editor_path,0o755)

    else:

    print()

# Pueue

![Pueue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Nukesor/images/main/pueue-v2.0.0.gif)

Pueue is a command-line task management tool for sequential and parallel execution of long-running tasks.

Simply put, it's a tool that **p**rocesses a q**ueue** of shell commands.
On top of that, there are a lot of convenient features and abstractions.

Since Pueue is not bound to any terminal, you can control your tasks from any terminal on the same machine.
The queue will be continuously processed, even if you no longer have any active ssh sessions.

## Features

- Scheduling
  - Add tasks as you go.
  - Run multiple tasks at once. You decide how many tasks should run concurrently.
  - Change the order of the scheduled tasks.

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser};
use std::env;
use std::path::Path;
use std::process::ExitCode;

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    // Check for -h/--help/version before clap? We'll let clap handle, but override help output?
    // For now, use clap with disabled help and manual help
    match run(args) {
        Ok(c) => ExitCode::from(c),
        Err(c) => ExitCode::from(c),
    }
}

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("pueue")
        .version("4.0.4")
        .about("Interact with the Pueue daemon\n\nUse the `--help` long form to get detailed help output on each subcommand!")
        .disable_help_flag(true)
        .disable_help_subcommand(true)
        .disable_version_flag(true)
        .arg(Arg::new("verbose").short('v').long("verbose").action(ArgAction::Count).help("Verbose mode (-v, -vv, -vvv)"))
        .arg(Arg::new("color").long("color").value_name("COLOR").default_value("auto").value_parser(["auto","never","always"]).help("Colorize the output; auto enables color output when connected to a tty"))
        .arg(Arg::new("config").short('c').long("config").value_name("CONFIG").help("If provided, Pueue only uses this config file"))
        .arg(Arg::new("profile").short('p').long("profile").value_name("PROFILE").help("The name of the profile that should be loaded from your config file"))
        .arg(Arg::new("help").short('h').long("help").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print help"))
        .arg(Arg::new("version").short('V').long("version").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print version"))
        .subcommand(Command::new("add").about("Enqueue a task for execution")
            .disable_help_flag(true)
            .arg(Arg::new("help").short('h').long("help").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Print help"))
            .arg(Arg::new("working-directory").short('w').long("working-directory").value_name("working-directory").help("Specify current working directory"))
            .arg(Arg::new("escape").short('e').long("escape").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Escape any special shell characters"))
            .arg(Arg::new("immediate").short('i').long("immediate").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Immediately start the task").conflicts_with_all(["stashed","delay"]))
            .arg(Arg::new("follow").long("follow").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Immediately follow").requires("immediate"))
            .arg(Arg::new("stashed").short('s').long("stashed").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Create the task in Stashed state"))
            .arg(Arg::new("delay").short('d').long("delay").value_name("delay").help("Prevents the task from being enqueued until 'delay' elapses."))
            .arg(Arg::new("group").short('g').long("group").value_name("GROUP").help("Assign the task to a group"))
            .arg(Arg::new("after").short('a').long("after").value_name("after").num_args(1..).value_parser(value_parser!(usize)).help("Start the task once all specified tasks have successfully finished"))
            .arg(Arg::new("priority").short('o').long("priority").value_name("PRIORITY").value_parser(value_parser!(i32)).help("Start this task with a higher priority"))
            .arg(Arg::new("label").short('l').long("label").value_name("LABEL").help("Add some information for yourself"))
            .arg(Arg::new("print-task-id").short('p').long("print-task-id").action(ArgAction::SetTrue).help("Only return the task id instead of a text"))
            .arg(Arg::new("COMMAND").required(true).num_args(1..).help("The command to be added"))
        )
        // ... more subcommands to be added
}

fn run(args: Vec<String>) -> Result<u8, u8> {
    // Manual help handling: check for -h/--help before subcommand?
    // For now, just try clap parsing
    let cli = build_cli();
    let m = cli.try_get_matches_from(&args);
    match m {
        Ok(matches) => {
            if matches.get_flag("help") {
                // Print main help (need to decide short vs long based on -h vs --help? Clap doesn't distinguish with SetTrue; need to check raw args)
                // For now, print long?
                print!("{}", include_str!("../help/main_long.txt"));
                return Ok(0);
            }
            if matches.get_flag("version") {
                println!("pueue 4.0.4");
                return Ok(0);
            }
            println!("parsed ok, verbose={}", matches.get_count("verbose"));
            Ok(0)
        }
        Err(e) => {
            let _ = e.print();
            Err(e.exit_code() as u8)
        }
    }
}

}

fn prog_name(args: &[String]) -> String {
    args.get(0).map(|s| Path::new(s).file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string()).unwrap_or(s.clone())).unwrap_or("executable".to_string())
}

fn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<u8, u8> {
    let prog = prog_name(args);
    // Manual help/version pre-check? Let clap handle parsing, but intercept help/version flags for hardcoded output
    let cli = build_cli();
    match cli.try_get_matches_from(args) {
        Ok(m) => {
            if m.get_flag("help") {
                let is_long = first_help_is_long(args, None);
                let txt = if is_long { include_str!("../help/main_long.txt") } else { include_str!("../help/main_short.txt") };
                print!("{}", txt.replace("executable", &prog));
                return Ok(0);
            }
            if m.get_flag("version") {
                print!("pueue 4.0.4\n");
                return Ok(0);
            }
            if let Some((sub, sub_m)) = m.subcommand() {
                return handle_subcommand(sub, sub_m, &m, args, &prog);
            } else {
                return handle_no_subcommand(&m, args, &prog);
            }
        }
        Err(e) => {
            let _ = e.print();
            Err(e.exit_code() as u8)
        }
    }
}

fn first_help_is_long(args: &[String], sub: Option<&str>) -> bool {
    // Find sub position if given, scan after it; else scan before subcommand for global
    let mut start_idx = 1;
    let mut end_idx = args.len();
    if let Some(s) = sub {
        // Find s in args
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
            if a == s {
                start_idx = i + 1;
                break;
            }
        }
    } else {
        // Global: scan until first non-option arg (subcommand) or --
        for (i, a) in args.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
            if a == "--" {
                end_idx = i;
                break;
            }
            if a.starts_with('-') && a.len() > 1 {
                continue;
            } else {
                end_idx = i;
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    for arg in args.iter().skip(start_idx).take(end_idx.saturating_sub(start_idx)) {
        if arg == "--" { break; }
        if arg == "--help" { return true; }
        if arg.starts_with("--help=") { continue; }
        if arg.starts_with("--") { continue; }
        if arg.starts_with('-') && arg.len() > 1 {
            // Check for combined -h, but need to handle -c/-p which take values? For simplicity, just look for 'h' char
            // But need to handle `-c value` where value could be "-h"? No, values after -c/-p are consumed, not flags.
            // Simplified: just check if arg contains 'h' as flag (like -h, -vh, -hv)
            // For args like "-c", "-p" (which require values), the next arg is value, not flags. Our simple scan doesn't handle that.
            // For help detection, it's okay to be approximate: look for 'h' in arg[1..] before '='?
            let part = arg[1..].split('=').next().unwrap_or("");
            for c in part.chars() {
                if c == 'h' { return false; }
            }
        }
    }
    false
}

    Command::new("pueue")
        .version("4.0.4")
        .about("Interact with the Pueue daemon\n\nUse the `--help` long form to get detailed help output on each subcommand!")
        .disable_help_flag(true)
        .disable_help_subcommand(true)
        .disable_version_flag(true)

use clap::{Arg, ArgAction, Command, value_parser, error::ErrorKind};
use std::env;
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

fn main() -> std::process::ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = env::args().collect();
    match run(&args) {
        Ok(c) => std::process::ExitCode::from(c),
        Err(c) => std::process::ExitCode::from(c),
    }
}

fn prog_name(args: &[String]) -> String {
    args.get(0).map(|s| Path::new(s).file_name().map(|n| n.to_string_lossy().to_string()).unwrap_or(s.clone())).unwrap_or("executable".to_string())
}

fn run(args: &[String]) -> Result<u8, u8> {
    let prog = prog_name(args);
    let cli = build_cli();
    match cli.try_get_matches_from(args) {
        Ok(m) => {
            if let Some((sub, sub_m)) = m.subcommand() {
                return handle_subcommand(sub, sub_m, &m, args, &prog);
            } else {
                return handle_no_subcommand(&m, args, &prog);
            }
        }
        Err(e) => {
            match e.kind() {
                ErrorKind::DisplayHelp => {
                    let txt = determine_help(args, &prog);
                    print!("{}", txt);
                    return Ok(0);
                }
                ErrorKind::DisplayVersion => {
                    print!("pueue 4.0.4\n");
                    return Ok(0);
                }
                _ => {
                    let _ = e.print();
                    return Err(e.exit_code() as u8);
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

fn build_cli() -> Command {
    Command::new("pueue")

import socket, os, tempfile, subprocess, threading, time, struct, sys
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp')
from cbor_codec import encode_cbor
def test(dark):
    tmpdir = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    sock_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "test.sock")
    cfg_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "pueue.yml")
    secret_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, "secret")
    open(secret_path,"w").write("testsecret")
    cfg_extra=f"client:\n  dark_mode: {str(dark).lower()}\n" if dark is not None else ""
    open(cfg_path,"w").write(f"shared:\n  unix_socket_path: {sock_path}\n  shared_secret_path: {secret_path}\n{cfg_extra}")
    srv = socket.socket(socket.AF_UNIX, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
    srv.bind(sock_path); srv.listen(1); srv.settimeout(5)
    def make_task(id, status):
        return {"id": id, "command": "echo hi", "original_command": "echo hi", "path": "/tmp", "label": None, "priority": 0, "group": "default", "envs": {}, "dependencies": [], "created_at": "2026-09-13T11:00:00Z", "status": status}
    queued={"Queued": {"enqueued_at": "2026-09-13T11:00:00Z"}}
    running={"Running": {"enqueued_at": "2026-09-13T11:00:00Z", "start": "2026-09-13T12:00:00Z"}}
    done_failed={"Done": {"enqueued_at": "2026-09-13T11:00:00Z", "start": "2026-09-13T12:00:00Z", "end": "2026-09-13T12:01:00Z", "result": {"Failed": 1}}}
    state_obj={"tasks": {0: make_task(0, queued), 1: make_task(1, running), 2: make_task(2, done_failed)}, "groups": {"default": {"status": "Running", "parallel_tasks": 1}}}
    def server():
        try:
            conn,_=srv.accept(); conn.settimeout(3)
            hdr=conn.recv(8); ln=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr)[0]
            body=b""
            while len(body)<ln: body+=conn.recv(ln-len(body))
            ver=b"fakeversion"; conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(ver))+ver)
            hdr2=conn.recv(8); ln2=struct.unpack('>Q',hdr2)[0]
            b2=b""
            while len(b2)<ln2: b2+=conn.recv(ln2-len(b2))
            payload=encode_cbor({"Status": state_obj}); conn.sendall(struct.pack('>Q',len(payload))+payload)
            conn.settimeout(1)
            try: conn.recv(8)
            except: pass
            conn.close()
        except: pass
        finally: srv.close()
    import threading
    st=threading.Thread(target=server); st.start(); time.sleep(0.1)
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","-c",cfg_path,"--color","always","status"], capture_output=True, timeout=10)
    st.join(timeout=5)
    print(f"dark={dark} => out={r.stdout[:3000]!r}")
    return r

for d in [None, True, False]:
    test(d)
    import time; time.sleep(0.3)

// ===== Protocol structs =====
use serde::{Serialize};
use chrono::{DateTime, Utc};

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "PascalCase")]
enum TaskSelection {
    TaskIds(Vec<usize>),
    Group(String),
    All,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
enum Signal {
    SigInt,
    SigKill,
    SigTerm,
    SigCont,
    SigStop,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct AddRequest {
    command: String,
    path: PathBuf,
    envs: HashMap<String, String>,
    start_immediately: bool,
    stashed: bool,
    group: String,
    enqueue_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>>,
    dependencies: Vec<usize>,
    priority: Option<i32>,
    label: Option<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
enum Request {
    Status,
    Add(AddRequest),
    Remove(Vec<usize>),
    Switch { task_id_1: usize, task_id_2: usize },
    Stash { tasks: TaskSelection, enqueue_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>> },
    Enqueue { tasks: TaskSelection, enqueue_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>> },
    Start { tasks: TaskSelection },
    Pause { tasks: TaskSelection, wait: bool },
    Kill { tasks: TaskSelection, signal: Option<Signal> },
    Send { task_id: usize, input: String },
    Env(EnvRequest),
    Group(GroupRequest),
    Log { tasks: TaskSelection, send_logs: bool, lines: Option<usize> },
    Clean { successful_only: bool, group: Option<String> },
    Parallel { parallel_tasks: usize, group: String },
    DaemonShutdown(ShutdownType),
    EditRequest(Vec<usize>),
    EditedTasks(Vec<EditableTask>),
    Restart { tasks: Vec<RestartTask>, start_immediately: bool, stashed: bool },
    Reset { target: ResetTarget },
    Stream { tasks: TaskSelection, lines: Option<usize> },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
enum EnvRequest {
    Set { task_id: usize, key: String, value: String },
    Unset { task_id: usize, key: String },
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
enum GroupRequest {
    List,
    Add { name: String, parallel_tasks: Option<usize> },
    Remove(String),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
enum ShutdownType {
    Graceful,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct EditableTask {
    id: usize,
    command: String,
    path: PathBuf,
    label: Option<String>,
    priority: i32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct RestartTask {
    task_id: usize,

fn handle_daemon_command(sub: &str, sub_m: &clap::ArgMatches, global_m: &clap::ArgMatches, _args: &[String], _prog: &str) -> Result<u8, u8> {
    let verbose = global_m.get_count("verbose");
    let loaded = load_config(global_m, verbose);
    let secret_path = get_secret_path(&loaded.shared);
    let secret = read_secret(&secret_path);
    // Determine suppress_warn for --json (for status/log/group with --json flag set, suppress version WARN)
    let suppress_warn = match sub {
        "status" => sub_m.get_flag("json"),
        "log" => sub_m.get_flag("json"),
        "group" => {
            // group --json (without subcommand) suppresses? What about group add/remove (no --json)? No suppress.
            // group with subcommand add/remove has no --json flag (only group list has --json). Good. So check if subcommand is None (list) and json flag set.
            if sub_m.subcommand().is_none() {
                sub_m.get_flag("json")
            } else {
                false
            }
        }
        _ => false,
    };
    let mut stream = connect_shared(&loaded.shared);
    do_handshake(&mut stream, &secret, verbose, suppress_warn);
    // Dispatch to per-command handler (which will log TRACE, send Request, recv Response, handle output)
    match sub {
        "add" => handle_add(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "remove" => handle_remove(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "switch" => handle_switch(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "stash" => handle_stash(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "enqueue" => handle_enqueue(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "start" => handle_start(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "restart" => handle_restart(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "pause" => handle_pause(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "kill" => handle_kill(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "send" => handle_send(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "edit" => handle_edit(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "env" => handle_env(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
        "group" => handle_group(&mut stream, sub_m, global_m, &loaded, verbose),
